statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-115557: the ssl module had no way to reject certificate chains that use the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys; the fix adds a built-in denylist of the SHA-256 digests of their public keys (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) and a certificate verification callback that rejects any certificate in the chain whose key is on the list. The check applies whenever the ssl module verifies the peer certificate (verify_mode CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED; ssl.create_default_context() sets CERT_REQUIRED for client-side contexts); a context set to CERT_NONE does not enforce verification results, so the denylist does not block those connections. Upstream issue: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160040, advisory: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/FNAJMZV6XQYLVPABNINDMF3VF66AYLW4/ and CVE record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557. The 3.11 backport is commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/af52b41afa4330fb38583db553631baa2f122f90 on the 3.11 branch, first released in 3.11.18; it adds the digest table Modules/_ssl/distrusted_spki.h and a verify callback in Modules/_ssl.c. There is no 3.10 release with the fix; DHI backports the same change onto 3.10.22. Checked the _ssl extension module (lib-dynload/_ssl.cpython-310-*.so) in the python-3.10 package for the first digest of that table, in every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8, x86_64 and aarch64, checksums verified against the repository index. The digest table is absent in every build before 3.10.22-r4 and present in 3.10.22-r4 and every later build, on both architectures. The range ends at 3.10.22-r4, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-115557: before CPython 3.11.18, the ssl module had no built-in way to reject TLS certificate chains through a set of compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys. The fix adds a denylist of the SHA-256 digests of eight public keys (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) and a verification callback that rejects any certificate whose key is on it whenever certificate verification is enabled (CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED); a context set to CERT_NONE does not verify certificates and is unaffected. Sources: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557 and https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160040 and the 3.11 branch commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/af52b41afa4330fb38583db553631baa2f122f90, which is first included in the v3.11.18 tag. We checked every package built from the python-3.11 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (pyc-3.11, python-3.11, python-3.11-dbg, python-3.11-dev, python-3.11-doc, python-3.11-gdbm, python-3.11-pyc, python-3.11-pycache-pyc0, python-3.11-pycache-pyc1, python-3.11-pycache-pyc2, python-3.11-tests) across every published build, 3.11.14-r0 to the current 3.11.18-r4 (24 builds), on x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against its index checksum. We searched every ELF file in those packages, including the members of static archives, for the eight key digests from the fix. The ssl module's _ssl extension module ships in python-3.11 in every build. In every build the same byte search finds the OpenSSL function names SSL_CTX_new and SSL_CTX_set_verify that the module imports, as a control. All eight digests are absent from it in every build up to 3.11.17-r1 and present in every build from 3.11.18-r0, on both architectures, and no other ELF file or archive member holds any of them. The _ssl debug files in the debug-information packages hold only debug data and symbol tables, with no copy of the module's data, so they were not counted either way. The range ends at 3.11.18-r0, the first build with the fix.

CVE-2026-115557: the ssl module had no way to reject certificate chains that use the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys; the fix adds a built-in denylist of the SHA-256 digests of their public keys (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) and a verify callback that fails verification of any certificate whose key is on that list, so a context that verifies certificates (CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED, including the default client context) rejects such chains; a context set to CERT_NONE does not verify certificates and is not protected. Checked the _ssl extension module (lib-dynload/_ssl.cpython-313-*.so) in the python-3.13 package for the eight digests in that table, in every build of the python-3.13 source published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4, x86_64 and aarch64, checksums verified against the repository index. All eight are present in 3.13.18-r0 and every later build, and none is present in any earlier build up to 3.13.17-r0, on both architectures. The range ends at 3.13.18-r0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-115557: before CPython 3.15.2, the ssl module had no built-in way to reject TLS certificate chains through a set of compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys. The fix adds a denylist of the SHA-256 digests of eight public keys (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) and a verification callback that rejects any certificate whose key is on it whenever certificate verification is enabled (CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED); a context set to CERT_NONE does not verify certificates and is unaffected. Sources: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557 and https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160040 and the 3.15 branch commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/36cd295f32fc9ba19399e01abee91231440a41dd, which is first included in the v3.15.2 tag. We checked every package built from the python-3.15 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (pyc-3.15, python-3.15, python-3.15-dbg, python-3.15-dev, python-3.15-doc, python-3.15-gdbm, python-3.15-pyc, python-3.15-pycache-pyc0, python-3.15-pycache-pyc1, python-3.15-pycache-pyc2, python-3.15-tests) across every published build, 3.15.0-r0 to the current 3.15.2-r4 (6 builds), on x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against its index checksum. We searched every ELF file in those packages, including the members of static archives, for the eight key digests from the fix. The ssl module's _ssl extension module ships in python-3.15 in every build. In every build the same byte search finds the OpenSSL function names SSL_CTX_new and SSL_CTX_set_verify that the module imports, as a control. All eight digests are absent from it in every build up to 3.15.0-r0 and present in every build from 3.15.2-r0, on both architectures, and no other ELF file or archive member holds any of them. The _ssl debug files in the debug-information packages hold only debug data and symbol tables, with no copy of the module's data, so they were not counted either way. The range ends at 3.15.2-r0, the first build with the fix.

CVE-2026-115557: the ssl module had no way to reject certificate chains that use the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys; the fix adds a built-in denylist of the SHA-256 digests of their public keys (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) and a certificate verification callback that rejects any certificate in the chain whose key is on the list. The check applies whenever the ssl module verifies the peer certificate (verify_mode CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED; ssl.create_default_context() sets CERT_REQUIRED for client-side contexts); a context set to CERT_NONE does not enforce verification results, so the denylist does not block those connections. Upstream issue: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160040, advisory: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/FNAJMZV6XQYLVPABNINDMF3VF66AYLW4/ and CVE record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557. The 3.11 backport is commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/af52b41afa4330fb38583db553631baa2f122f90 on the 3.11 branch, first released in 3.11.18; it adds the digest table Modules/_ssl/distrusted_spki.h and a verify callback in Modules/_ssl.c. There is no 3.10 release with the fix; DHI backports the same change onto 3.10.22. Checked the _ssl extension module (lib-dynload/_ssl.cpython-310-*.so), which ships in libpython-3.10-stdlib up to 3.10.20-9 and in libpython-3.10-minimal from 3.10.20-10, for the first digest of that table, in every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Debian 13 repository, 3.10.20-0 to 3.10.22-8, amd64 and arm64 (3.10.20-0 to 3.10.20-2 were published as architecture-independent packages), checksums verified against the repository index. The digest table is absent in every build before 3.10.22-3 and present in 3.10.22-3 and every later build, on both architectures. The range ends at 3.10.22-3, the first published build with the fix.

Upstream added the denylist in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160040 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e9bf2cf84eebf838a1edaa1c648c2b36345b99d3), first released in CPython 3.14.10; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/FNAJMZV6XQYLVPABNINDMF3VF66AYLW4/; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557. Checked the _ssl extension module in every published build, 3.14.5-0 to 3.14.10-6, of the DHI Debian 13 python-3.14 packages (the standard library is in libpython-3.14-minimal and libpython-3.14, or libpython-3.14-stdlib in the earliest builds) on amd64 and arm64 for the distrusted-key table and SPKI check the fix adds. 3.14.5-0 to 3.14.8-0 lack the fix; 3.14.10-0 is the first published build that has it and is built from the upstream 3.14.10 release, and every later build carries it.

CVE-2026-115557: before CPython 3.15.2, the ssl module had no built-in way to reject TLS certificate chains through a set of compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys. The fix adds a denylist of the SHA-256 digests of eight public keys (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) and a verification callback that rejects any certificate whose key is on it whenever certificate verification is enabled (CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED); a context set to CERT_NONE does not verify certificates and is unaffected. Sources: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557 and https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160040 and the 3.15 branch commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/36cd295f32fc9ba19399e01abee91231440a41dd, which is first included in the v3.15.2 tag. We checked every package built from the python-3.15 source in the DHI Debian 13 repository (libpython-3.15, libpython-3.15-dbgsym, libpython-3.15-dev, libpython-3.15-dev-dbgsym, libpython-3.15-minimal, libpython-3.15-minimal-dbgsym, libpython-3.15-stdlib, python-3.15, python-3.15-dev, python-3.15-minimal, python-3.15-minimal-dbgsym) across every published build, 3.15.0-0 to the current 3.15.2-7 (9 builds), on amd64 and arm64, each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. We searched every ELF file in those packages, including the members of static archives, for the eight key digests from the fix. The ssl module's _ssl extension module ships in libpython-3.15-minimal in every build. In every build the same byte search finds the OpenSSL function names SSL_CTX_new and SSL_CTX_set_verify that the module imports, as a control. All eight digests are absent from it in every build up to 3.15.0-0 and present in every build from 3.15.2-0, on both architectures, and no other ELF file or archive member holds any of them. The _ssl debug files in the debug-information packages hold only debug data and symbol tables, with no copy of the module's data, so they were not counted either way. The range ends at 3.15.2-0, the first build with the fix.
